scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The house is migrating. Help me choose where it should rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Houses don't migrate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This one packed its chimney. We should support its journey.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where could it go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Somewhere with good foundations and a watering hole.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The house is migrating south. Help me redirect it before we lose the driveway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The surveyor says subsidence. He's bringing concrete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Concrete traps it halfway across the road. Tell him we're planning a route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His truck's blocking the road already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Ask him to lead slowly toward the empty plot. It needs a guide.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 recruits help choosing a destination, but A3 asks for support without making migration a useful explanation.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 counters B2 with a packed chimney; A5 answers B4 but adds an unsupported watering hole.

relationship.evidence: B2 disputes migration and B4 asks where; neither gives B a practical stake.

heightening.evidence: A5 supplies a destination preference without increasing A1's commitment or consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies a migrating house, but no immediate household problem explains the request.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's packed chimney is economical, while A5's watering hole adds animal imagery rather than useful logic.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 turns B2's concrete repair into an obstacle to migration; A5 recruits B to arrange a guide for the house.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 supplies concrete, which A3 says would trap the house; B4 supplies the truck, which A5 repurposes as its guide.

relationship.evidence: B2 brings the surveyor's ordinary repair plan, and B4 identifies an immediate obstruction that changes A's tactic.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4's blocked road into a plan to enlist the surveyor and relocate the house to an empty plot.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a threatened driveway; B2's surveyor and B4's truck give the exchange concrete, playable objects.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'It needs a guide' economically completes the conversion of B4's obstruction into migration assistance.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 introduces concrete; A3 rejects it specifically as something that would immobilize a migrating house.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 puts the surveyor's truck in the road; A5 makes that truck the house's guide.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 recruit B into making practical decisions through the impossible migration explanation.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 expands redirecting the house into a coordinated relocation using the ordinary repair crew.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D151 recruits B to use an impossible explanation because it offers a workable account of what to do next.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: D155 requests one premise-dependent choice; D151 seeks shared use of an explanatory framework.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A3 asks B to support the house's journey; revised A3 and A5 make migration govern the surveyor's concrete and truck.

records.recommendedEdit: Replaced decorative migration with a new driveway-and-surveyor situation. Internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3 makes migration useful), logic 5 (A3 uses concrete; A5 uses B4's truck), relationship 4 (B2 brings a credible remedy), heightening 4 (A5 recruits the surveyor as guide), specificity 4 (A1 supplies the driveway problem), brevityWit 4 (A5 earns its guide idea): 90.
records.remainingConcern: The house's ability to follow a truck is an additional assumption, though consistent with A's sincere migration premise. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The house following a guide remains a comic assumption; actors must sincerely treat it as the available solution.
records.alternativeComparison: Unlike D151-single-b's workplace negotiation and B's helpful offer, this alternative converts an ordinary repair plan and obstruction into migration logistics.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Treat the kettle's complaints as advice. Help me answer it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only says boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A clear agenda. Ask what resources it needs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: More water?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. We're already collaborating with the impossible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office kettle's on strike. Help me negotiate before the clients arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've filled it twice. It still won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then water isn't its grievance. Tell it we'll stop leaving it alone after meetings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take it into the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Give it my chair. A seat at the table should get us tea.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 invites consultation with the kettle, but A5 explicitly labels the impossible instead of demonstrating its usefulness.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 makes B2's boil into an agenda; A5 acknowledges B4's proposed water.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 supply literal kettle functions without a separate need or meaningful cost.

heightening.evidence: A5 announces collaboration rather than developing B4's helpful water proposal.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a kettle but no occasion or practical reason to answer its complaints.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'collaborating with the impossible' explains the exercise instead of remaining natural character speech.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 interprets failed filling as an unresolved grievance; A5 recruits B into giving the striking kettle workplace representation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's repeated filling eliminates water as A3's grievance; B4's meeting offer becomes A5's proposal to give the kettle A's chair.

relationship.evidence: B2 has already tried to restore tea service; B4 actively offers inclusion in the meeting rather than merely challenging A.

heightening.evidence: A5 escalates B4's offer to carry the kettle into a meeting by surrendering A's own chair to it.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an office kettle failure before clients arrive; A3 connects its grievance to being abandoned after meetings.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'A seat at the table should get us tea' follows the negotiation premise, although the idiom is familiar.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 reports that water has not worked; A3 treats that as evidence that the grievance concerns companionship.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 offers meeting access; A5 specifies the concession of A's chair as the means to secure tea.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A treats a labor dispute as the useful explanation for appliance failure and draws B into negotiating.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 moves from promising company to sacrificing A's place in the meeting.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D151 makes A enlist B in treating a bizarre explanation as a useful basis for joint problem-solving.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: D158 redirects questions toward tasks without needing B to adopt an explanation; D151 actively recruits that adoption.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A3 interprets boiling as an agenda; revised A3 interprets failed refilling as evidence of a grievance and A5 proposes representation.

records.recommendedEdit: Added a new office-client deadline and replaced the explanatory ending. Internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3 advances the strike explanation), logic 5 (A3 uses failed filling; A5 uses B4's meeting offer), relationship 4 (B2 has already tried helping), heightening 4 (A5 yields A's chair), specificity 4 (A1 establishes office visitors), brevityWit 4 (A5's seat earns its double meaning): 90.
records.remainingConcern: The final phrase is slightly polished for spontaneous speech, but its practical bargain is earned. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The office-strike metaphor is familiar; the personal chair concession carries most of the final turn's freshness.
records.alternativeComparison: D151-single-a reroutes an outside repair operation; this version uses cooperative colleagues and a personal concession to the kettle.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Catch one drop of tomorrow in this cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone needs to stay in today to record the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What counts as tomorrow's water?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me whether it tastes ahead of schedule.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This tap gives you whatever you ask for. Ask for tea while I hold a cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not using my good china for that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll hold a saucepan. You ask.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for a biscuit instead. If one comes out, we won't need your tongue as equipment.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 delegates catching tomorrow, but neither A1 nor A5 supplies a practical way to distinguish tomorrow's water.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 responds to B2's refusal; A5 answers B4's measurement question with another undefined metaphor.

relationship.evidence: B2 resists doing the test and B4 reasonably asks what would count as evidence.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves to tasting but does not make the experiment more actionable or consequential.

specificity.evidence: A1 provides a cup without a source of water or a playable experimental setting.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's recorder excuse is concise; A5's 'ahead of schedule' obscures the requested action.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks B to activate the impossible tap; A3 keeps the testing action with B despite changing the receptacle.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's china objection produces A3's saucepan; B4's tasting refusal produces A5's visibly identifiable biscuit, though tea appearing would already provide evidence.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects valued china and B4 limits personal involvement; A3 and A5 accommodate both boundaries.

heightening.evidence: A5 upgrades the requested output from liquid to a solid biscuit in response to B4's refusal to taste.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a tap experiment with a held cup; B2 and A3 make the domestic equipment immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'I'll hold a saucepan. You ask' is economical; A5's tongue-as-equipment joke follows the testing logic but is slightly elaborate.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 refuses good china, so A3 substitutes a saucepan while retaining B as the person who asks.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 refuses tasting, so A5 requests a biscuit that can establish the claim without tasting.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 repeatedly recruit B to perform the practical activation of the bizarre tap.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 makes the tap produce a solid object while preserving the experiment and accommodating B's boundary.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D152 makes A recruit B to perform an observable first test that could substantiate an extraordinary claim.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: D155 requests accommodation of an accepted premise; D152 requests an action whose result supplies evidence for the premise.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 asks B to test the tap's response to a spoken request; A5 changes the requested output to something visibly distinguishable without tasting.

records.recommendedEdit: Replaced the rejected tomorrow-water inference with a new request-responsive kitchen tap. Original firstPass remains unchanged. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A1 assigns B the evidentiary request), logic 5 (A3 replaces B2's china; A5 makes B4's tasting refusal determine the biscuit test), relationship 4 (B2 protects property and B4 limits participation), heightening 4 (A5 advances from liquid to an unmistakable solid output), specificity 4 (A1 supplies tap and cup), brevityWit 4 (A5's tongue-as-equipment follows the refusal): 90. Five spoken ABABA turns; the test remains proposed rather than resolved.
records.remainingConcern: The tea experiment already offers visible evidence; A5's revised test is motivated but not strictly necessary. No rewrite needed for acceptance.
records.writerReservation: The biscuit is a stronger demonstration than tea, but it depends on taking A1's 'whatever' literally; no successful result is supplied or presumed.
records.alternativeComparison: This alternative uses domestic cooperation and equipment concessions; D152-single-b negotiates physical testing and confidence in a bridge's load capacity.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Test the invisible bridge with your umbrella before I step on it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why my umbrella?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It reaches farther than your confidence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It went straight through.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good data. Try the next invisible plank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's an invisible bridge across this ditch. Tap for it with your umbrella before I cross.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use your walking stick.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yours extends. You can test it without leaving the bank.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probe. But a surface isn't proof it'll hold you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Slide your picnic basket onto it first. Leave my lunch inside; I want a convincing weight.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks B to probe an invisible bridge; A5 persists after a negative result, slightly shifting toward unfalsifiable belief.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's umbrella question and A5 requests another probe because B4 reports no contact.

relationship.evidence: B2 questions use of their property, but A3 substitutes a confidence insult for a persuasive answer.

heightening.evidence: A5 requests another plank test without materially increasing commitment or refining the test.

specificity.evidence: A1 clearly establishes a crossing, an umbrella and A's desire to test before stepping.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's confidence line is compact but weakly motivated by B2's equipment question.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 recruits B to probe the invisible bridge, and A5 recruits B again for a practical load test.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 suggests A's stick; A3 explains the umbrella's reach. B4 distinguishes surface from strength; A5 supplies a weighted basket test.

relationship.evidence: B2 resists supplying the equipment and B4 insists on an adequate test; A3 and A5 must address those specific concerns.

heightening.evidence: B4's load-bearing objection moves A5 from probing for existence to risking the picnic basket and A's lunch.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes the ditch, bank-side test and umbrella; A5 provides a concrete next action with a picnic basket.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 efficiently justifies the equipment choice; A5's insistence on leaving lunch inside earns its joke through the need for weight.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 proposes A's walking stick; A3 gives a specific reason B's extending umbrella is better.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 says a surface cannot establish load capacity; A5 asks B to slide a loaded basket onto it.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1 and A5 assign B concrete tests that could establish the impossible bridge's existence and usefulness.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 increases the test's commitment from touching an invisible surface to placing possessions on it.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D152 makes A enlist B to take the first practical step toward verifying a bizarre claim.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Simply sending B into danger would express risk avoidance; this exchange asks B to obtain evidence with objects before anyone crosses.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 requests an umbrella probe, A3 explains its reach, and A5 answers B4's evidentiary objection with a proposed load test.

records.recommendedEdit: Kept the ditch and extending umbrella but replaced the procedural ending with B's distinction between contact and support. Original firstPass remains unchanged. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A1 and A5 delegate concrete tests), logic 5 (A3 answers B2's stick proposal; A5 directly addresses B4's load objection), relationship 4 (B4 contributes a credible standard for the crossing), heightening 4 (A5 adds a loaded basket and A's own lunch), specificity 4 (A1 establishes the ditch and equipment), brevityWit 4 (A5 treats lunch as a serious experimental contribution): 90. Five spoken ABABA turns leave the experiment open.
records.remainingConcern: A basket cannot establish that the bridge supports a person, but it is a coherent incremental test. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A picnic basket could establish load-bearing capacity without establishing that the bridge supports a person; the dialogue proposes an initial test, not sufficient clearance to cross.
records.alternativeComparison: Compared with D152-single-a's household accommodations, this alternative makes B an active methodological skeptic and gives A a personal stake through the lunch.

cards.title: Choose the Real Impossibility
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which of two incompatible explanations will govern what everyone does next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Are we shrinking or is the room growing? Choose before we move the sofa.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does it matter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One requires smaller movers, the other a larger van.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're shrinking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Stop ordering ordinary-sized biscuits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we move the sofa: are we shrinking while the room stays normal, or is the room growing while we stay normal?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever gets this move finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shrinking means call full-sized help. Growing means hurry before the door gets farther away. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're shrinking. I'll call my brother.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him to bring tweezers. He'll need to collect us afterward.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands a choice, but shrinking people and a growing room could coexist, weakening the required incompatibility.

responseLogic.evidence: A3's mover and van sizes do not clearly follow the alternatives; A5 abandons moving the sofa for biscuits.

relationship.evidence: B2 questions relevance and B4 chooses, but B has no further moving constraint.

heightening.evidence: A5's biscuit order changes subjects instead of increasing commitment to the sofa plan.

specificity.evidence: A1 naturally gives the pair a shared sofa-moving task.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 is efficient, but A5's ordinary-sized biscuits are a detachable consequence joke.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 explicitly offers mutually exclusive size changes, and A3 makes B choose between calling help and hurrying.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's wish to finish with two action plans; A5 equips the brother B4 chooses, though the sofa's relative size is unstated.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the move finished; B4 selects an explanation and volunteers a specific helper.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4's rescue choice encompass collecting the shrinking movers themselves with tweezers.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes moving a sofa, and B4's brother gives A5's tweezers request a concrete recipient.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's tweezers follow the selected shrinking explanation and increase its personal consequence without an unrelated joke.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 prioritizes finishing the move; A3 translates both explanations into ways to act on that priority.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 selects shrinking and calls a brother; A5 specifies equipment for that helper under the selected explanation.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A requires an incompatible explanatory choice to govern the shared moving plan.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 extends the implications from moving furniture to retrieving the movers.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D154 makes B choose between incompatible accounts so one account determines the group's next actions.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Offering two fanciful possibilities is insufficient unless choosing one commits the group to a different course.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A1 leaves the explanations jointly possible; revised A1 fixes what stays normal and A3 assigns each exclusive account a different plan.

records.recommendedEdit: Preserved the sofa move and made the alternatives exclusive. Internal reread: fidelity 5 (A1 specifies incompatible accounts), logic 5 (A3 addresses B2's deadline; A5 uses B4's brother), relationship 4 (B wants the move finished), heightening 4 (A5 adds rescuing the movers), specificity 4 (A1 gives the shared task), brevityWit 4 (A5's tweezers follow shrinking): 90.
records.remainingConcern: The sofa's participation in the size change is unspecified, leaving a small practical ambiguity. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The explicit exclusions make A1 longer than conversational ideal, though the entire scene remains under 75 words.
records.alternativeComparison: D154-single-b uses deadline and supply constraints to select a buffet plan; this version turns B's family assistance into personal rescue.

cards.title: Choose the Real Impossibility
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which of two incompatible explanations will govern what everyone does next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is gravity late, or are we early?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Neither makes sense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only one explains whether lunch should wait.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Gravity's late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the sandwiches somewhere they can land safely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sandwiches are floating. Is gravity late for lunch, or has it resigned? We need a serving plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The guests arrive in five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Late means plates underneath. Resigned means string on every sandwich. Which are we doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Late. We haven't enough string.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then fetch the deep plates. We may get the whole buffet at once.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 offers gravity being late or people being early, but those accounts are neither clearly incompatible nor operationally distinct.

responseLogic.evidence: A5 uses B4's choice of late gravity, while A3 never explains how being early would change lunch.

relationship.evidence: B2 rejects the premise and B4 selects an answer without revealing a practical concern.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes a landing precaution, but lunch waiting remains only vaguely established in A3.

specificity.evidence: A1 does not identify floating objects or a setting; lunch appears only in A3.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's landing sandwiches are concise, but the missing physical setup makes the image harder to play.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks whether gravity is temporarily absent or permanently gone; A3 assigns plates or string to those incompatible explanations.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's five-minute deadline prompts A3's immediate serving options; B4 selects temporary absence, leading A5 to prepare for gravity's return.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects the guests' arrival schedule, and B4 makes a resource-based decision because string is scarce.

heightening.evidence: A5 develops B4's choice into a simultaneous buffet drop requiring deep plates.

specificity.evidence: A1's floating sandwiches, B2's arriving guests and B4's string shortage make the serving problem immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'whole buffet at once' economically follows the return-of-gravity explanation selected in B4.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 imposes an imminent arrival; A3 turns speculation into a choice between two executable serving plans.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 chooses late gravity because string is insufficient; A5 commits to catching the food when gravity returns.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A forces selection between temporary and permanent absence, each with different practical consequences.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 scales the chosen plate plan from individual sandwiches to the entire buffet arriving together.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D154 makes a selected impossible explanation govern a concrete collective plan.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: D151 recruits belief in one useful explanation; D154 requires a decision between two competing explanations with different consequences.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 ties late gravity to plates and resigned gravity to string, so B4's choice directly determines A5's equipment request.

records.recommendedEdit: Replaced the unclear early/late distinction with temporary absence versus resignation, establishing a new buffet setting. Internal reread: fidelity 4 (A1 frames competing work statuses), logic 5 (A3 uses B2's deadline; A5 develops B4's late choice), relationship 4 (B4 supplies a shortage), heightening 4 (A5 anticipates simultaneous landing), specificity 5 (A1 and B2 make service playable), brevityWit 4 (A5 earns the buffet image): 86.
records.remainingConcern: B2's deadline informs urgency more than the particular equipment choices, and deep plates provide only a modest escalation. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The incompatibility relies on ordinary meanings of being late for an expected duty versus having quit that duty.
records.alternativeComparison: This alternative is cooperative event planning under time and supply pressure; D154-single-a brings in outside family help and escalates to rescuing the participants.

cards.title: Act as If It’s True
cards.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If the ceiling's hungry, put its breakfast on the top shelf.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it isn't hungry?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll have been polite. Lift the bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I add a spoon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. That's a useful kind of belief.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ceiling's hungry. Turn the breakfast tray upside down so it can eat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's our last porridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep half for us. Just turn its bowl over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll use the tray to catch anything it drops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Hold it under the light fitting; that's where it dribbled yesterday.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks for breakfast positioned for a hungry ceiling, although A5 comments on belief rather than requesting a premise-dependent choice.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's hunger objection; A5 directly accepts B4's spoon suggestion.

relationship.evidence: B4 offers practical help, but B2 gives little indication of what B personally needs.

heightening.evidence: A5 approves the spoon without adapting the action to the ceiling or increasing commitment.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies breakfast and a top shelf; A3 supplies a liftable bowl.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'useful kind of belief' states an abstract lesson instead of continuing the concrete scene.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks B to invert breakfast for a hungry ceiling; A3 preserves that concrete choice while reducing the food sacrificed.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's last-porridge objection causes A3's half portion; B4's catching tray causes A5 to identify the ceiling's dribbling location.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects their breakfast and B4 offers a cleanup solution, giving A both a limit and useful collaboration.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4's sensible catching precaution into evidence of a familiar ceiling-feeding routine.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes breakfast with a tray; A3 specifies a bowl and A5 locates the mess under the light fitting.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'that's where it dribbled yesterday' earns the domestic detail through B4's offer to catch drops.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies a scarce shared meal; A3 reduces the ceiling's portion while retaining the inversion request.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 offers the tray as a catcher; A5 tells B exactly where catching is needed.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Turning a bowl upside down as feeding makes sense only within A's hungry-ceiling premise.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 makes the ceiling a recurring dependent with a known feeding mess.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D155 makes A request a concrete choice whose practical sense depends on the impossible premise being true.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: D152 seeks a test of truth; D155 asks for accommodation of the premise without needing proof.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A1 places food for a ceiling; revised A1 requests inversion for feeding, and A5 treats B's catch-tray offer as normal care.

records.recommendedEdit: Kept ceiling breakfast and replaced the abstract closing with a specific feeding arrangement. Internal reread: fidelity 5 (A1 requests upside-down service), logic 5 (A3 preserves B2's porridge; A5 locates B4's tray), relationship 4 (B protects shared breakfast), heightening 4 (A5 adds established care knowledge), specificity 4 (A1 supplies tray and meal), brevityWit 4 (A5's dribbling develops feeding): 90.
records.remainingConcern: How the inverted porridge reaches the ceiling is left to the impossible premise; the interaction itself remains clear. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A5 supplies new history about the light fitting; it should read as practical knowledge rather than a separate invented joke.
records.alternativeComparison: This version uses resource bargaining and a helpful cleanup offer; D155-single-b uses a dinner-hosting paradox and labeling, with substantially less coherent temporal logic.

cards.title: Act as If It’s True
cards.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Reserve a chair for tomorrow's visitor as though they've already accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody's replied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow works ahead. Leave one seat free.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What name goes on it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write reserved until time catches up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sister's bringing her future self to dinner. Reserve two chairs for her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only saved her one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use mine. I won't make either of her eat standing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put the extra chair beside hers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'tomorrow' on its place card. I need to know which one can tell me how tonight went.

cards.title: Say You Saw It Too
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit noticing the impossible detail before you reveal how much you believe it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did the soup wave at you too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are you staring at the bowl?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm waiting for an independent witness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It raised a noodle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. I was beginning to feel rude not waving back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you send this soup back, did you notice anything moving?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm complaining about cold noodles. What did you see?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me whether one waved. I need your word before I explain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It waved me closer. I'm still not eating it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll understand why I've ordered it lunch. Could you ask whether it wants your bread?

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 requests a witness before A5 reveals that A regards returning the soup's wave as a matter of politeness.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 explains the staring queried in B2; B4's raised noodle supplies the observation that releases A5's admission.

relationship.evidence: B2 notices A's awkward behavior and B4 offers concrete corroboration, allowing A to disclose a more embarrassing belief.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from asking whether soup waved to acknowledging a felt obligation to wave back.

specificity.evidence: A1's soup and B2's bowl establish an immediately playable meal; B4 specifies the noodle's movement.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's concern about rudeness follows the wave and exposes A's sincere social logic without explanation.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 solicits an observation, A3 explicitly withholds explanation until B confirms, and A5 reveals the extent of belief only after B4 admits the wave.

heightening.evidence: After B4 confirms the wave, A5 reveals A has already ordered the noodle lunch and recruits B to ask about bread.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes soup about to be returned; B2 supplies cold noodles, and A5 builds a playable restaurant interaction from lunch and bread.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'I've ordered it lunch' efficiently reveals hidden commitment; A3's 'I need your word before I explain' states the withholding tactic somewhat explicitly.
